# Melaya

> Melaya is a visual builder for high-trust AI agents, with Device Control as its flagship. Build, run, and orchestrate multi-agent pipelines (agents with scoped tools, per-agent model and prompt, RAG, static context, memory, evaluations, human-in-the-loop, scheduling/triggers, templates, and sub-agents), and put those agents in control of real mobile devices. Built by an operator, for operators. 1,500+ tools, 100+ specialized subagents, 20+ AI providers, secure connectors, per-workflow RAG with isolated vector stores, and a full audit trail. Trading (via Melaya Labs) is one upcoming vertical built on the same agent infrastructure, paired with a Rust-native engine over 70+ venues.

Melaya is a standalone agentic platform headquartered in the United Arab Emirates, solo-built by Antoine Roche, who spent the previous decade shipping production trading systems at BNP Paribas CIB (EQD eCommerce, 2018-2022), SingularityDAO (product manager, DeFi yield vaults and on-chain analytics, 2021-2025), and Singularity Venture Hub (head of trading operations, HFT market making and execution tooling, 2025-2026).

Design philosophy: agents should not be loose chatbots with unlimited powers. They need scoped tools, clear permissions, secure credentials, cost tracking, audit logs, data-quality monitoring, and human approval where risk is high. Melaya applies operational discipline to every agent workflow.

## The three products

- Agent Builder (live today) - the orchestration studio and the base platform. Drag agents, tools, and models onto a canvas, wire them, and schedule/run/replay multi-agent pipelines. Scoped tools, sub-agents, per-agent model and prompt, RAG, static context, memory, evaluations (loopPolicy), human-in-the-loop, and templates. 1,500+ scoped tools, 100+ subagents, 20+ model providers. Anything an LLM can reason about, an agent runs alongside your team.
- Device Control (flagship, live today) - AI agents that operate a real Android phone the way a person does: read the screen via the accessibility tree, then tap, type, swipe, and navigate between apps. No per-app integration and no vendor API, driven by the same agent infrastructure (scoped tools, memory, HITL, scheduling), with human approval on every sensitive action.
- Trading (Melaya Labs vertical, upcoming) - one application built on the agent infrastructure: multi-agent trading crews paired with a Rust-native engine that normalizes market data and order routing across 70+ venues, exposed as one unified REST + WebSocket API. Every order waits for your approval.

## Core capabilities

- 1,500+ agentic tools across web, code, data, ops, communication, files, cloud, social, RAG, device actions, an MCP bridge, and (for the trading vertical) market data and order placement.
- 100+ specialized subagents with prebuilt crews for research, analysis, execution, and review.
- Bring-your-own model across 20+ AI providers: Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Google Gemini, NVIDIA, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI Grok, Moonshot Kimi, Zhipu, Qwen, Cerebras, Groq, SambaNova, Upstage, Reka, MiniMax, and OpenRouter, plus local models via Ollama and LM Studio.
- Per-workflow RAG: isolated vector stores with hybrid BM25 + dense retrieval.
- Secure connectors: AES-256-GCM envelope encryption, managed-vault secrets, per-user credential isolation.
- Full observability: pipeline run logs, tool-call traces, model invocation cost and token tracking, error reasons.
- Human-in-the-loop: per-tool approval gates, approval queue, scoped permissions and roles.
- Multi-tenant: project-scoped RBAC, per-project credential vaults, isolated execution environments.

## Agent Builder (the base platform, live today)

- Pipeline-as-config: define a multi-agent pipeline as one JSON config, then create, run, track, and collect its outputs through the SDK or REST. The server regenerates the runnable pipeline deterministically from the structured config.
- Steps: agent, parallel (fan-out then merge), condition (branch on prior output), and loop (iterate until a stop condition or cap).
- Per-agent configuration: model/provider, system prompt override, scoped toolkit, human-approval tools, RAG opt-in, static-context opt-in, per-agent loopPolicy and cost cap.
- Sub-agents (crews): an agent can delegate to a nested agent exposed as a callable tool, or be built from a registered crew factory.
- Knowledge: vector RAG (isolated store), static context (whole documents pinned into the prompt), and persistent cross-session memory. Local-only residency keeps documents on your runner.
- Evaluations: a loopPolicy (off / observe_only / enforce) judges an agent's output and decides whether to continue, retry, or stop.
- Cost caps, scheduling and triggers, build-with-AI (the architect drafts and self-corrects a config), and reusable templates.
- Execution target: cloud or your own runner; force_local_runner pins the whole pipeline to your runner even for cloud models.

## Device Control (flagship, live today)

- AI agents operate a real Android phone like a human: ORIENT (read the screen tree), then act (tap, type, swipe, navigate), act-and-observe on every step.
- Flat async tool set: reading tools (phone_get_screen_tree, phone_screenshot, phone_current_app, phone_list_apps, phone_app_playbook) and acting tools (phone_click_text, phone_click_id, phone_tap, phone_swipe, phone_input_text, phone_open_app, phone_batch, and global navigation).
- Works with apps that have no public API, using the accessibility tree (or a screenshot for canvas/OpenGL screens).
- Pairing mints a durable, revocable device token; a paired phone long-polls a per-user queue and executes actions through an Android AccessibilityService.
- On-device app allowlisting: an agent can only touch apps the user explicitly authorized, enforced on the device itself.
- Human-in-the-loop on publishing: posting a comment or creating a post is HITL-gated on the device, with a universal per-user STOP kill flag.
- Server-side app playbooks: per-app navigation knowledge injected into the tool response so agents act like they already know the app.
- Operates a sleeping phone (Doze): the command path is heartbeat-aware so scheduled runs drive an idle phone unattended.

## Trading vertical (Melaya Labs, upcoming)

- One application built on the agent infrastructure above: autonomous, multi-agent trading crews of specialized personas (Macro, TA, Quant, Sentiment, Risk, Portfolio, Execution) that research, size risk, and execute.
- Human-in-the-loop approval on every order; only the execution persona places trades, and it pauses for operator approval. Every decision is audited.
- Server-managed stop-loss / take-profit, cadence (time schedules, market-event triggers, or hybrid), and reactive sidecars (drawdown, macro blackout, funding flip, liquidation cascade).
- Three ways to trade: paper (sim broker), managed strategies (a custom Rhai script or a full agent_crew), and direct live trading.
- Native backtesting on the same Rust engine that runs the strategy live, including grid sweep and random sample, plus AI parameter optimization with a human gate.
- Launchable via API: crews launch through POST /api/v1/strategies as strategyType "agent_crew" (paper or live). HITL is currently always-on for trading crews.

## Unified market & trading API (Melaya Labs vertical)

- One normalized REST + WebSocket interface over 70+ venues, powered by an in-house Rust engine.
- REST base: https://api.melaya.org - WebSocket base: wss://wss.melaya.org
- Market data: ticker, order book, OHLCV, public trades, exchange status/time, markets, currencies.
- Derivatives: funding rates, funding-rate history, open interest, open-interest history, instrument constraints.
- Streaming: live ticker, order book, OHLCV, public trades, and cross-exchange liquidations.
- Trading: account balances, orders, positions, fills, live order placement (create/cancel/amend/close, leverage & margin controls), agent-driven strategies, paper (sim-broker) trading, and native backtesting on the Rust engine. Reads, paper, and backtests need only the `mk_` key; live order placement also requires a connected exchange key.

## SDKs

- One `mk_` platform key unlocks the full surface across three planes: agents (pipelines, sub-agents, tools, RAG, memory, evaluations, HITL, scheduling, templates), device control (pair, drive on-screen actions, run device crews), and platform (projects, credentials/connectors, teams, observability), plus the upcoming trading vertical (market data, paper + live trading, strategies, backtesting, streaming).
- Authentication: API keys prefixed `mk_`, sent as `Authorization: Bearer mk_...` on every REST request. Public WebSocket streams instead take `?apiKey=mk_...` on the wss URL; private WebSocket streams use a short-lived `?wsTicket=`.
- Official SDKs in 9 languages (TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, Kotlin, C#/.NET, Ruby, PHP) wrap the full surface with one identical API each.
